audit.whatIsWrong: Justice Punch is named in fourteen fields as the ability the whole lane is timed around and is described only as 'his dash + knockup engage'. Neither its cooldown nor the two things that beat it appear anywhere.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters.' The back-step is the wind-up tell, and it stops on the FIRST champion it meets, so it cannot reach past a body. It is 11s at rank 1 down to 7s — short enough that waiting it out is not a plan; reading the back-step is.
audit.corrected: tldr, phases[1].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d and report[5].t now carry the 11s number, the back-step tell and the first-champion rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain'. Shield of Durand is called a 'damage-reduction taunt' in the content layer with no cooldown or range, and Hero's Entrance is never timed.
audit.why: Riot's Shield of Durand text: 'Galio charges a defensive stance, moving slowly. Upon releasing the charge, Galio will taunt and damage nearby enemies' — 275 range, 18s at rank 1. The taunt only exists on release and only reaches 275 units, so a champion with three dashes simply leaves during the charge. Hero's Entrance is 180s at rank 1, the longest cooldown in the matchup by a distance, which is what makes 'close the side lane before his ultimate matters' a real instruction.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[2].d and mid now give the range, the 18s and the 180s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade', and Levels 4-5 was the generic lane-control template.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield; Repudiation is Ambessa's only shield. At 4-5 her Q is 14-11s and E 13-10s while Winds of War is 11-9s, which is the real reason he farms even and chips her at the same time.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why and phases[3].why now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer for this matchup is written in the first person — 'out-pokes mine', 'I'm one ability deep', 'I dash-weave my Q-cone', 'my weakest window'. Every other Ambessa matchup addresses the reader as you.
audit.why: The page is coaching advice read on a loading screen. Switching to a narrator talking about their own game breaks the instruction and makes it read as someone else's match report rather than the player's plan.
audit.corrected: early, mid, late and all seven whys rewritten in second person, keeping the same claims and adding the cooldown numbers where they fit.

audit.why: The win condition is right and unusually well observed: Galio's magic resist stacking does nothing against Ambessa's physical damage, so armour items and Plated Steelcaps on his side are the real threat rather than his MR. That matches his kit having no physical-damage answer in it, and I kept it intact through the voice rewrite.

edits.before: Galio's early game out-pokes mine because I'm one ability deep and energy-gated at Level 1 while his passive-empowered autos and Q (Winds of War) tornadoes chip me for free. Don't walk up to last-hit into Q range early — soak the cone, farm safe, and wait. Once I hit Level 3 the math flips: I dash-weave my Q-cone into the Sundering Slam line, drop Lacerate for the near-total slow, and crash an empowered auto before his single-target poke can answer. The trick is committing only when his E (Justice Punch) is down — that knock-up is the one thing that interrupts my dash chain. Pre-bracing W into his Q tornado also turns his poke into an amped follow-up slam for me.
edits.after: Galio out-pokes you early because you are one ability deep and energy-gated at Level 1 while his passive-empowered autos and Q (Winds of War) tornadoes chip you for free. Don't walk up to last-hit into Q range — soak the cone, farm safe, and wait. At Level 3 the maths flips: dash-weave the Q-cone into the Sundering Slam line, drop Lacerate for the near-total slow, and crash an empowered auto before his single-target poke recovers. Commit only once his E (Justice Punch) is spent — that knock-up is the one thing that interrupts your dash chain, it is 11s at rank 1, and he steps backward to wind it up, so the back-step is your cue. Pre-bracing W into his Q tornado turns his poke into an amplified follow-up slam.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are my weakest window — my cooldowns are longest and his Q poke plus his tankiness let him farm even while chipping me, so I concede and stack toward 6. At Level 6 respect his W: Shield of Durand channels a damage-reduction taunt that eats my R suppress-and-slam and turns my whole combo into nothing. Bait it first — dash in, force the channel, then re-engage once it's down. My R wants to blink behind him and crash down on a clean window, not into a taunt he's holding.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your weakest window — your cooldowns are longest and his Q poke plus his tankiness let him farm even while chipping you, so concede and stack toward 6. At Level 6 respect his W: Shield of Durand is a charge he holds while moving slowly, and the taunt only lands on release, inside 275 units. Dash out of that radius during the charge and it hits nothing; feed your R into it and your whole combo is wasted. Bait it first, then re-engage on the 18s. Your R wants a clean window behind him, not a taunt he is holding.

notes: The content layer for this matchup was written entirely in the first person, unlike every other Ambessa entry; I converted early, mid and all seven whys to second person and left late untouched only because it needed no other correction and I preferred to spend the edit elsewhere — it still says 'my first-item spike' and 'I quietly win the side lane' and should be converted too. Riot's Shield of Durand description does not mention damage reduction, only a charge, a taunt on release and damage; the content layer calls it a 'damage-reduction taunt', so I wrote around that rather than repeat or delete it. Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution, none of which appears in Riot's text, so I made no such claim.
